sourcing.title: Somali resins, from the tree to the lot
sourcing.text: How frankincense and myrrh are harvested in Somalia, and how they are sorted and checked before export.

sections.title: Somali natural resin origins
sections.text: The mountains of northern Somalia have supplied aromatic resins for thousands of years. Frankincense trees grow on the dry, rocky slopes of this region, often on limestone, where few other crops can survive.

sections.title: Boswellia and Commiphora sourcing
sections.text: Frankincense comes from Boswellia trees. In Somalia, trade centres on Boswellia carterii, known locally as Beeyo, and Boswellia frereana, known as Maydi. Myrrh, known as Malmal, comes from Commiphora species, mainly Commiphora myrrha.

sections.title: Traditional harvesting
sections.text: Harvesters make shallow cuts in the bark, and the tree seeps a milky sap that hardens into resin tears over several weeks. The tears are collected by hand. This skilled work is usually passed down through families.

sections.title: Product grading
sections.text: Grades reflect the size, colour, clarity and cleanliness of the resin. Grade names differ across the trade, so we confirm exactly what each grade means in your quotation, rather than relying on a label.

sections.title: Sorting and cleaning
sections.text: After drying, resin is cleaned of bark and debris, then sorted by hand into grades. Careful sorting is what turns a harvest into a consistent commercial lot.

sections.title: Quality assurance
sections.text: Lots are visually checked for grade, cleanliness and consistency before packing. If your market requires laboratory analysis or other documents, tell us at the quotation stage so we can arrange what is needed.

sections.title: Responsible sourcing
sections.text: Frankincense trees face real pressure from over-tapping, grazing and climate stress. Fair treatment of harvesters and rest periods for the trees are essential to the future of this trade, and we want to be part of that effort.

sections.title: Traceability where available
sections.text: Where the information is available, we can share the region and collection details of a lot. Tell us your requirements early, as records vary by harvest and supply chain.

sourcing.notice: Tree and bark photos on this page are representative. Where a photo was taken outside Somalia, its caption says so. See the image credits for sources.

about.title: A Somali trading company, established in 2003
about.text: Adde General LLC connects Somalia's natural resins with buyers around the world.
about.history: Adde General LLC was established in 2003. Since then, the company has built its experience in trade from Somalia, working in a region known for its frankincense and myrrh for thousands of years. Today we source, supply and export these resins to international markets from our presence in Puntland.
about.mission: To supply natural resins from Somalia reliably and honestly, while creating lasting value for buyers and for the communities who harvest them.
about.vision: To be a trusted name in Somali natural resins for international buyers.

values.title: Integrity
values.text: We say only what we can support, and we confirm details in writing.

values.title: Quality
values.text: We sort with care and agree each specification with the buyer.

values.title: Respect
values.text: For harvesters, for the trees, and for our customers' time.

values.title: Long-term thinking
values.text: We value lasting relationships over one-off transactions.

about.experience: Over two decades of doing business in Somalia has taught us how to work with local supply networks, plan around harvest seasons and communicate clearly with partners abroad.
about.commitment: Every buyer gets a clear reference number, direct contact with our team and straightforward answers on grades, availability and shipping.
about.presence: Puntland, in north-east Somalia, is home to frankincense-growing mountains and the port of Bosaso on the Gulf of Aden. Our presence here puts us close to the origin of the resins we supply.
about.captionTrees: Trees at Karin, near Bosaso, Somalia

industries.title: Natural resins for many industries
industries.text: Frankincense and myrrh have uses across many sectors. Tell us your application and we will discuss suitable products and grades.

items.title: Pharmaceuticals
items.text: Boswellia and myrrh have long histories in traditional medicine and are subjects of continuing research. Pharmaceutical buyers should share their specification and testing requirements with us at quotation stage.

items.title: Nutraceuticals
items.text: Boswellia is a widely used ingredient in herbal extracts and dietary supplements. We can discuss resin supply for extraction and formulation.

items.title: Perfumes and Fragrances
items.text: Frankincense and myrrh add depth, warmth and balsamic character to fine fragrance, as resins or as materials for extraction.

items.title: Aromatherapy
items.text: Distillers use these resins to produce essential oils for aromatherapy, where botanical species strongly shapes the aroma.

items.title: Cosmetics and Personal Care
items.text: Resin extracts and oils appear in skincare, soaps and personal care formulations that favour natural ingredients.

items.title: Incense and Religious Use
items.text: Frankincense has been burned in religious ceremonies for millennia and remains central to many traditions and incense makers today.

items.title: Natural Product Manufacturers
items.text: Makers of natural products, from candles to chewing resins and traditional remedies, can source raw resin by grade and volume.

industries.disclaimer: These descriptions outline general uses of these materials. They are not medical or regulatory claims. Buyers are responsible for compliance in their own markets.
